subject: app-rdef
title: APP.RDEF.------P.PROG.
description: Diagram in SD(SY)-47 (Spectacle-Diversion Syndrome, Level One) accompanying Braxton's diagnostic that 'all of the signs for real change have solidified and the question now is which way will events take us … the most basic factor to induce the need for positive change is the awareness of extended information.' (C)APP-RDEF (the concept of apparent redefinition) is crossed with P-PROG (positive progression): the question is what apparent-redefinition produces when crossed with positive-progression — when the late-seventies progressional weight is 'isolating the dynamics of composite perception.' POL-P (political particulars) feeds into P-PROG from above. CRTF-D (creative-dynamic) sits between subject and partner on the upper register. IST-F (interior-source functionalism) anchors the upper-right margin. P-PROG itself is centrally crossed. W-DY (world dynamics) connects to INFO-AF-B (information-affinity basis) via a *dashed* edge — the only mediated/conditional relation in the diagram, marking Braxton's caution that world-dynamics' link to information-affinity-basis is uncertain. RT-ALGN (reality alignment) feeds upward into P-PROG from the lower-left. CUL-INFO-F (culture-information functionalism) anchors the lower-center via another dashed edge. Structural argument: apparent-redefinition crossed with positive-progression is the diagnostic for the late-seventies situation — apparent-redefinition is what the dominant culture offers as 'change,' while positive-progression is what actually obtains. The diagram's two dashed edges (W-DY→INFO-AF-B and P-PROG→CUL-INFO-F) are load-bearing: they expose that the link between progression and culture-information is mediated, conditional — exactly the gap that 'extended information awareness' must close to enable real change.
